I farm with two things in mind: steady grain first, then cash income, and I keep the work manageable because there are only two people in my household and I am 62. On my 12 mu, I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the backbone of my farm and it fits my experience and irrigation conditions. I will put 8 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 8 mu, and I will keep 4 mu in cotton for cash income and to spread risk. I will use better seed on all three crops because I want stable emergence, more uniform growth, and less chance of losing yield. I have well irrigation, so I will use water at the key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. I will not push inputs to the highest level because labor is limited and I prefer a stable, manageable crop over chasing a little extra yield with more risk and more work. For wheat I will fertilize enough to secure tillers and grain filling, irrigate at the important stages, and keep tillage simple with rotary work. For maize I will use hybrid seed, feed it more nitrogen than the other crops, irrigate in hot dry periods, and keep pests under control with a few timely sprays. For cotton I will keep the area smaller because it takes more hands, but I will still grow it for cash, with moderate fertilizer, several irrigations, and a few pesticide applications because insects can quickly damage the crop.
